messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED] 
Age: 68 
Gender: Male 
Admission Date: [REDACTED] 
Discharge Date: [REDACTED] 

Medical History:
The patient presented with left-sided abdominal pain, early satiety, fatigue and 7 lbs weight loss for seven weeks. Past medical history significant for hypertension, emphysema and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) with successful treatment with sofosbuvir and ribavirin.

Hospital Course:
On admission to the emergency department, the patient's vitals were stable. His clinical examination was unremarkable, except for left-sided abdominal tenderness. Abdominal ultrasound showed splenomegaly and MRI of the abdomen confirmed multiple hypoenhanced lobulated masses in the spleen. SPECT showed heterogeneous splenic uptake with areas of photopenia related to splenic masses, and liver biopsy showed chronic hepatitis. Bone marrow biopsy ruled out lymphoma and JAK2 mutation was negative. After performing splenic biopsy, DLBCL was diagnosed, and the patient was started on R-CHOP. 

After six cycles of R-CHOP, the patient's PET scan showed complete remission on PET and decrease in spleen size. However, six months later, he presented with left lower quadrant pain and splenic biopsy showed a relapse of DLBCL. Due to his poor performance status, the patient was started on palliative lenalidomide and rituximab.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged and will follow up for further treatment in the outpatient setting. 

Follow-up Instructions:
The patient was instructed to consult with the oncology team for further management.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the episode is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), primarily involving the spleen and relapsed after R-CHOP, treated with palliative lenalidomide and rituximab. It belongs to chapter C (neoplasms), and DLBCL is coded to C83 (non-follicular lymphoma, with C83.3 for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma).

CODE: C83
